profile.name: Natural spin turn
profile.tagline: A ballroom dance step used in the waltz to advance and turn.
profile.insight: The natural spin turn advances a couple 5⁄4 of a turn down the line of dance and serves as a stepping stone toward learning pivots.
profile.profile: The natural spin turn is a ballroom dance step used in the waltz, typically used to advance a couple 5⁄4 of a turn down the line of dance. It consists of the first half of a natural turn followed by an under-turned pivot. An underturned variation allows leaders to navigate a corner by reducing total rotation. It is also considered an intermediary step toward learning pivots.
profile.profile_long: The natural spin turn is a ballroom dance step used in the waltz. It is typically used to advance a couple 5⁄4 of a turn down the line of dance. Structurally, the step consists of the first half of a natural turn followed by an under-turned pivot. The natural spin turn is also considered an intermediary step toward learning pivots. A useful variation is the underturned spin, which allows a leader to navigate a corner. This variation is identical to the natural spin turn but rotates 3⁄8 of a turn on the pivot on beat 4 instead of 1⁄2, and 1⁄4 of a turn on counts 4 to 6 instead of 3⁄8, reducing total rotation by 1⁄4 of a turn.
